Dear Wanderer, as I write, I picture your face.
Some days ago, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the local school. There, I saw the children sitting upright with solemn faces, buried in their books, not even noticing our approach.
Curious, I wondered what marvelous texts could hold the attention of these usually restless youngsters. Upon asking, I learned they were reading books you had gifted them not long ago.
When I inquired what made these books so special, the children eagerly chimed in, and I realized you had thoughtfully selected different books for each child—truly a labor of love. Hearing that I knew you, they begged me to convey their gratitude.
Yet, when pressed to articulate their thanks, the little ones grew shy and tongue-tied. So, I suggested they put their thoughts into writing, and here they are, sealed within this letter. Rest assured, I did not peek!
Oh, and the children also entrusted me with a few drawings, inspired by the books they read. They insisted you, with your discerning taste, would appreciate their masterpieces.
Ha Ha, it seems for any future tasks involving children, you, dear Wanderer, are the one to call upon.
